### The Infection Occurred Before the Third Day of the Stay {#sec-problem-details-20}

An infection which occurred before the third day of the stay — day 1 or day 2 of it — was most probably already present when the infant came to the department, and the surveillance does not record it. For an infant transferred or readmitted to the department the NeoIPC Surveillance Protocol sets exactly this cut-off: an infection counts as hospital-acquired only where the symptoms begin on or after day 3 of the stay, the day of admission counting as day 1. This report applies that cut-off to every admission, since an infection before the third day of a stay is most probably not acquired in the department; an exception the NeoIPC support team has accepted keeps a record out of these findings.

Please delete the forms of the infections which are not hospital-acquired under this definition (see @sec-solution-12), and correct the infection date (see @sec-solution-7) or the admission date (see @sec-solution-6) only where one of them was entered as the wrong date.
